_schema: Open provenance/attribution issues found during translation, keyed by paper id. Each: slug, severity, summary, evidence, action_needed. These were surfaced by the translation agents and converted from internal halt-reports into tracked issues (Sept 2026). They are NOT resolved.

138.summary: A run of source scans filed with this paper belongs to a different paper, so one passage of the translation is missing.
evidence: Scan pages 7-15 (printed pp. 375-383) carry verso running-headers reading 'Werner Kornfeld' while the recto running-title reads 'Abhaengigkeit der metamorphotischen Kiemenrueckbildung usw.'

Their subject matter is transplantation and developmental mechanics (induction in transplants, synchrony/heterochrony, germ-cell determination, heteroplastic skin grafts), not tadpole gill resorption.
The string 'Kiemenrueckbildung' appears only in the running-title header, never in the body text of those pages.
The title page of the gill-resorption paper is absent from the scan set.
The translator declined to translate those pages rather than emit the wrong paper's text.
138.action_needed: Obtain the correct scans for the missing printed pages and translate them. Separately, settle the author's forename: the catalog says only 'Kornfeld', the translation's own byline reads 'Werner Kornfeld', and the halt-report treats the gill paper as by 'Walter Kornfeld'. The title page is needed to decide.

_153_koppanyi.summary: The pages translated under Koppanyi's eye-replantation title are in fact a study by Auguste Jellinek on rats learning to discriminate feeding vessels by colour.
evidence: 'Die Replantation von Augen. VII.' is the collected-volume series title, not this paper's title.
The page-top author byline on every page reads 'Auguste Jellinek'.
Content: sighted, blind and transplanted-eye rats compared on a colour-discrimination learning task.
The translation faithfully renders what is actually on the pages (printed pp. 89-95).
_153_koppanyi.action_needed: Decide whether this should be catalogued under Auguste Jellinek as her own contribution to the eye-replantation series. Jellinek is named in Mueller (ed.), Vivarium (MIT Press 2017) among the institute's women scientists and currently has only a stub biography on the Authors page; this may be her paper.
